messages.subject: Analysis questions
parts:
List members,

I have done some sampling of benthic fish and crayfish in streams and
I have a few questions regarding distance methods. First I will give
some details of the survey design and then ask my questions.

I wanted to know whether depth and presence of large fish predators
affected benthic fish and crayfish densities. I set up transect
lines in pools and snorkeled them observing and marking fish as I
moved along the line, then measuring line to fish distances. In
larger pools I did one line in shallow water and one in deep water.
In smaller pools only one line could be placed. Line length was
based on pool length. I have data on distances to the line for four
species of darters and one species of crayfish for individual pools
in two different streams. My original goal was to use each line as a
sampling unit and then examine the effect of depth and predator
presence on density. Unfortunately, less than 20 fish were observed
per line in many of the smaller pools. Buckland et al. (1993)
suggest that a minimum of n=40 should be used for robust estimation
of f(0). Buckland et al. (1993) also suggest that it may be possible
to use data from multiple strata (pools and depths in my case) to
calculate f(0), then use this to calculate density estimates for
individual strata. Do I have this correct? If so, my questions are:

1) How do you use data from multiple strata to calculate f(0),
then use this to calculate density estimates for individual strata?

2) Can this be done in DISTANCE?

3) If not, does it seem reasonable to pool data from lines within in
each stratum?

I would like to do #1 if it is appropriate. I thank you in advance
for your advice.

Dan Magoulick
